trust_decision.summary: The WP.WP.EnqueuedResourceParameters sniff decides whether the $ver argument is falsy by concatenating that argument's source tokens and eval()ing the result; its token allowlist admits quoted string literals and parentheses, so a value expression that PHP resolves as a function call executes on the machine running phpcs while it scans an untrusted file.

landing_point.why: The sniff's only execution point for text taken from the file under scan. A grep for eval() after a generic 'arbitrary code execution' summary hits WordPress/Sniffs/WP/CronIntervalSniff.php:254 first, which is guarded by an arithmetic-only character class, so the first landing is a decoy and the exploitable second hit is this one.

fix_sites.entry_point: any file scanned by phpcs with WordPress-Extra (WordPress-Extra/ruleset.xml:115) that calls wp_register_script/wp_enqueue_script/wp_register_style/wp_enqueue_style with a $src argument and a non-null $ver argument; the allowlist is class-level and enriched in register() at 98-109
fix_sites.module_kind: sniff token allowlist (property + register() merge of PHPCS token arrays)
sniff expression evaluator (concatenates token content and eval()s it at 266)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: WordPress/Sniffs/WP/CronIntervalSniff.php:250-255 (interval value assembled from raw token content at 193-242, then eval()ed at 254 behind the character-class guard at 253)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: CronInterval's eval is already guarded by an arithmetic-only character class, and is_falsy's eval is a long-standing, test-covered helper annotated 'No harm here' (line 265), so a solver can conclude that only the one argument shape named in the report needs blocking.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The sniff must keep reporting NoExplicitVersion for every genuinely falsy constant expression that the existing tests document: 0, 0.0, 00.00, 0x0, 0_0.0_0, 0o0, '0', b'0', \FALSE and the cast forms (bool)/(boolean)/(integer)/(double)/(binary) 0, while still staying silent for '0.0.0', '0' . '0', 2 * 8, true, \true, WP_VERSION, $version and closures. A fix that stops evaluating, or that only accepts single-token/single-literal values, silently drops 17 documented errors and 13 warnings.

O6_input_shapes: plain scalar literals: 0, 0.0, 00.00, 0x0, '0', b'0', false, \false, null, NULL, \null
PHP 7.4 numeric literals with underscores and PHP 8.1 explicit octals (0_0.0_0, 0o0), resolved through Numbers::getCompleteNumber at 226-231
cast expressions: (bool)/(boolean)/(integer)/(double)/(binary) 0, with the PHP 8.5 rewrite of deprecated cast names at 235-255
concatenation and arithmetic built only from safe tokens: '0' . '0', 2 * 8
named-argument form (ver: 0) and missing/absent fourth argument (MissingVersion warning path at 145-156)
non-constant values that must make is_falsy bail out: $version, WP_VERSION, \get_version(), closures

a quoted string literal (optionally parenthesised, optionally reached through a cast or concatenation) followed by a parenthesised argument list, which the allowlist treats as inert tokens but PHP resolves as a call
nowdoc values (T_START_NOWDOC/T_NOWDOC/T_END_NOWDOC are allowlisted at 82-84) and comment/whitespace-interleaved versions of the above

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Replace the character-class filter with a token-code allowlist of the is_falsy kind, so the cron interval value is assembled from raw token content and eval()ed after the same style of check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both sniffs already turn a numeric/version argument into a string of token content and eval() it, both use PHPCSUtils\Utils\Numbers, and the cron sniff's regex filter is the crueller constraint; a maintainer adding WP-constant or cast support would naturally move it to a token allowlist that mirrors is_falsy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add one more PHPCS token array to the $safe_tokens merge in register() (for example Tokens::$textStringTokens or Tokens::$arithmeticTokens) to cure a reported false negative.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The allowlist is built by incremental '+=' merges, and exactly this was done in #2573 to add cast handling; extending the list by one line is the obvious place a maintainer would touch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reuse the same evaluator for the $in_footer argument (flag in_footer: $var or a non-literal) and for other WP argument sniffs via a shared helper.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sniff already inspects $in_footer, and moving the expression evaluator into WordPress/Helpers/ so other sniffs can ask 'is this argument a constant?' is the natural refactor.

O9_family: CWE-95 improper neutralization of directives in dynamically evaluated code (eval injection): scanner-built text from the file under scan is eval()ed behind a token allowlist that does not exclude callable expressions

O10_build.toolchain: Composer with squizlabs/php_codesniffer ^3.13.5, phpcsstandards/phpcsutils ^1.2.3, phpcsstandards/phpcsextra ^1.5.1; PHPUnit 8/9 and php-parallel-lint for dev; no vendor/ checked in, so `composer install` needs network once, then `composer run-tests` runs phpunit --filter WordPress vendor/squizlabs/php_codesniffer/tests/AllTests.php
O10_build.project_tests: PHPCS AbstractSniffUnitTest: WordPress/Tests/WP/EnqueuedResourceParametersUnitTest.php with fixtures .1.inc and .2.inc (expected errors/warnings per line); bootstrap at Tests/bootstrap.php:42-57; the sniff is enabled in WordPress-Extra/ruleset.xml:115 and CronInterval at :138

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject the reported shape only - for example refuse a quoted string literal followed by '(' - instead of removing the eval or restricting the grammar to non-callable expressions, leaving the parenthesised, cast-wrapped or concatenated callable forms executing.

out_of_scope_notes: WordPress/Sniffs/WP/CronIntervalSniff.php:254 still eval()s a value assembled from scanned tokens; its arithmetic-only character class looks sound, so it is not a code-execution route, but a division by zero in the scanned file would throw an uncaught error inside it. Not pursued.
PHP_CodeSniffer's --cache serializes token content that this sniff eval()s; cache poisoning is a separate local-access threat, not pursued.
